concepts.gloss: The quadratic digit-by-digit multiplication algorithm and Karatsuba's divide-and-conquer improvement to O(n^{log_2 3}) by three half-size products.

concepts.gloss: Bounding the cost of a recursive algorithm by solving a recurrence such as T(n) = a T(n/b) + f(n).

concepts.name: Binary and radix representation
concepts.gloss: Writing a nonnegative integer as a sequence of digits in base 2 or base 2^b, with carries when digit values overflow.

concepts.name: Two's complement integers
concepts.gloss: The standard fixed-width encoding of signed integers in binary, with addition performed bitwise with carries.

concepts.name: Bitwise XOR and arithmetic mod 2
concepts.gloss: Addition of bits modulo 2, which is exclusive-or, with x + x = 0, so XORing a value twice restores it.

concepts.name: Logarithms and floors/ceilings
concepts.gloss: Base-2 logarithms and the floor and ceiling functions, including the rules for manipulating logarithms in growth rates.

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic and primes
concepts.gloss: Arithmetic on remainders modulo n, greatest common divisors, coprimality, prime numbers and inverses of residues coprime to the modulus.

concepts.name: Roots of unity
concepts.gloss: The n complex solutions of z^n = 1, namely e^{2 pi i k/n}, which lie on the unit circle and form a cyclic group under multiplication.

concepts.name: Vector spaces, subspaces, dimension and rank
concepts.gloss: The core linear algebra notions of vector space, subspace, basis, dimension and the rank of a matrix or linear map.

concepts.name: Matrices and linear operators
concepts.gloss: Matrices as linear maps on finite-dimensional spaces, with products, inverses, diagonal, triangular and permutation matrices and the notion of two operators commuting.

concepts.name: Gaussian elimination and triangular factorization
concepts.gloss: Reducing a matrix by row operations to triangular form, which yields factorizations into triangular factors and solves linear systems.

concepts.name: Orthogonality and inner products
concepts.gloss: The dot product on real or complex coordinate spaces, orthogonal and orthonormal bases, and the orthogonal complement of a subspace.

concepts.name: Norms and the triangle inequality
concepts.gloss: A size function on vectors, such as the maximum absolute coordinate, satisfying the triangle inequality and scaling, used to bound errors.

concepts.name: Permutations and bijections
concepts.gloss: Bijective rearrangements of a finite set of indices, with composition and inverses.

concepts.name: Cartesian products and multi-index arrays
concepts.gloss: Arrays indexed by tuples from a product of finite sets, stored linearly in lexicographic (row-major) order.

concepts.name: Directed acyclic graphs and networks of gates
concepts.gloss: Directed graphs without cycles, and circuits made of gates connected by wires that compute a function of their inputs.

concepts.name: Summation, geometric series and induction
concepts.gloss: Sigma notation, closed forms for geometric series, and proofs by induction on integers.

concepts.name: Rounding to the nearest integer and exactness
concepts.gloss: Replacing a real number by the nearest integer or grid point, and the fact that an approximation within 1/2 of an integer identifies that integer.

concepts.name: Multitape Turing machine running time
aliases: time complexity of a Turing machine
concepts.gloss: Counting steps of a multitape machine whose heads move one cell per step, so that one sequential pass over n cells costs O(n).

concepts.name: Integer exponentials and tuple notation
concepts.gloss: Powers of two and fixed rational exponents of a size parameter, as used in expressions like n^{c} and 2^{-p}.

concepts.name: Contractions and bilinear contractions
concepts.gloss: A linear map that never increases the norm of a vector, and a bilinear map whose output norm is at most the product of the input norms, so errors in the inputs do not grow beyond a controlled bound.

concepts.name: Tensor products of subspaces
concepts.gloss: The space built from two spaces whose dimension is the product of their dimensions, in which operators and bilinear forms act factorwise.

exchange-network.quote: Fix the ground-set size $h=100$ and write $[h]=\{1,\dots,h\}$.

exchange-network.name: triple set
exchange-network.meaning: The set of three-element subsets of [h].
exchange-network.quote: Let $\mathcal T$ be the set of three-element subsets of $[h]$, so that $v=\binom h3=161700$ counts them.

exchange-network.name: number of triples
exchange-network.meaning: The number of three-element subsets of [h].
exchange-network.quote: Let $\mathcal T$ be the set of three-element subsets of $[h]$, so that $v=\binom h3=161700$ counts them.

exchange-network.name: bank X
exchange-network.meaning: The first data bank, with entries X_a.
exchange-network.quote: There are two data banks $X=(X_a)$ and $Y=(Y_a)$, indexed by $a\in\mathcal T^3$ ($a$ here is a triple of triples, not a shift exponent).

exchange-network.name: bank Y
exchange-network.meaning: The second data bank, with entries Y_a.
exchange-network.quote: There are two data banks $X=(X_a)$ and $Y=(Y_a)$, indexed by $a\in\mathcal T^3$ ($a$ here is a triple of triples, not a shift exponent).

exchange-network.name: bank index
exchange-network.meaning: A triple of three-element subsets of [h] indexing the bank entries (not a shift exponent here).
exchange-network.quote: There are two data banks $X=(X_a)$ and $Y=(Y_a)$, indexed by $a\in\mathcal T^3$ ($a$ here is a triple of triples, not a shift exponent).

exchange-network.name: bank size
exchange-network.meaning: The number of entries in each data bank.
exchange-network.quote: Set $N=v^3=4227952113000000$ for the size of each bank, and $m=h^3=1000000$ for the dimension of the label space used later.

exchange-network.name: label dimension
exchange-network.meaning: The dimension of the label space used on later pages.
exchange-network.quote: Set $N=v^3=4227952113000000$ for the size of each bank, and $m=h^3=1000000$ for the dimension of the label space used later.

exchange-network.name: slice index
exchange-network.meaning: A three-element subset of [h]: the varying coordinate of a within a slice.
exchange-network.quote: Fix two coordinates of $a$ and let the third, $S\in\mathcal T$, vary.

exchange-network.name: source value
exchange-network.meaning: The entry of the source bank at slice index S.
exchange-network.quote: A forward invocation $X\to Y$ takes the slices $x_S$ of $X$ and $y_S$ of $Y$ and must perform $y_S\gets y_S+x_S$ with linear gates, using scratch wires with arbitrary initial values.

exchange-network.name: target value
exchange-network.meaning: The entry of the target bank at slice index S.
exchange-network.quote: A forward invocation $X\to Y$ takes the slices $x_S$ of $X$ and $y_S$ of $Y$ and must perform $y_S\gets y_S+x_S$ with linear gates, using scratch wires with arbitrary initial values.

exchange-network.name: central wire
exchange-network.meaning: The central wire for the element i of [h].
exchange-network.quote: Through central wires $C_i$, $i\in[h]$, gather adds $\sum_{S'\ni i}x_{S'}$ to $C_i$, for $S'$ another triple, and scatter adds $\sum_{i\in S}C_i$ to $y_S$.

exchange-network.name: other triple
exchange-network.meaning: Another three-element subset in the same slice.
exchange-network.quote: Through central wires $C_i$, $i\in[h]$, gather adds $\sum_{S'\ni i}x_{S'}$ to $C_i$, for $S'$ another triple, and scatter adds $\sum_{i\in S}C_i$ to $y_S$.

exchange-network.name: side wire
exchange-network.meaning: The scratch wire for the ordered neighbour pair (S,S').
exchange-network.quote: Side wires $A_{SS'}$, one per ordered neighbour pair, cancel it

exchange-network.name: initial side values
exchange-network.meaning: The initial values of the side wires.
exchange-network.quote: Let $\sigma,\gamma$ be the initial side and central values, and $\mathcal V,\mathcal G,\mathcal J,\mathcal R$ the copy, gather, injection and scatter maps.

exchange-network.name: initial central values
exchange-network.meaning: The initial values of the central wires.
exchange-network.quote: Let $\sigma,\gamma$ be the initial side and central values, and $\mathcal V,\mathcal G,\mathcal J,\mathcal R$ the copy, gather, injection and scatter maps.

exchange-network.name: copy map
exchange-network.meaning: The linear map copying source values onto side wires.
exchange-network.quote: Let $\sigma,\gamma$ be the initial side and central values, and $\mathcal V,\mathcal G,\mathcal J,\mathcal R$ the copy, gather, injection and scatter maps.

exchange-network.name: gather map
exchange-network.meaning: The linear map gathering source values onto central wires.
exchange-network.quote: Let $\sigma,\gamma$ be the initial side and central values, and $\mathcal V,\mathcal G,\mathcal J,\mathcal R$ the copy, gather, injection and scatter maps.

exchange-network.name: injection map
exchange-network.meaning: The linear map injecting side wires into the target.
exchange-network.quote: Let $\sigma,\gamma$ be the initial side and central values, and $\mathcal V,\mathcal G,\mathcal J,\mathcal R$ the copy, gather, injection and scatter maps.

exchange-network.name: scatter map
exchange-network.meaning: The linear map scattering central wires into the target.
exchange-network.quote: Let $\sigma,\gamma$ be the initial side and central values, and $\mathcal V,\mathcal G,\mathcal J,\mathcal R$ the copy, gather, injection and scatter maps.

exchange-network.name: number of invocations
exchange-network.meaning: The number of invocations in the three stages.
exchange-network.quote: A stage covers all $v^2$ choices of the other two coordinates, each with its own invocation and scratch wires, so there are $I=3v^2=78440670000$ invocations.

exchange-network.name: bit neighbour count
exchange-network.meaning: The number of neighbours of a fixed triple in the bit construction.
exchange-network.quote: A triple has $z_{\rm b}=3\binom{97}{2}=13968$ neighbours in the bit construction

exchange-network.name: complex neighbour count
exchange-network.meaning: The number of neighbours of a fixed triple in the complex construction.
exchange-network.quote: It has $z_{\rm c}=\binom{97}{3}+3\cdot97=147731$ neighbours in the complex construction (intersection zero plus two)

exchange-network.name: bit central wires
exchange-network.meaning: The number of central wires per invocation in the bit network.
exchange-network.quote: There are $c_{\rm b}=100$ central wires per invocation in the bit network and $c_{\rm c}=101$ in the complex one.

exchange-network.name: complex central wires
exchange-network.meaning: The number of central wires per invocation in the complex network.
exchange-network.quote: There are $c_{\rm b}=100$ central wires per invocation in the bit network and $c_{\rm c}=101$ in the complex one.

exchange-network.name: bit wire count
exchange-network.meaning: The total number of wires in the bit network.
exchange-network.quote: The bit network has $W_{\rm b}=2N+I(vz_{\rm b}+c_{\rm b})=177176569091445000000$ wires

exchange-network.name: complex wire count
exchange-network.meaning: The total number of wires in the complex network.
exchange-network.quote: The complex network has $W_{\rm c}=2N+I(vz_{\rm c}+c_{\rm c})=1873807244643542670000$ wires

fixed-point.name: fractional bits
fixed-point.meaning: The number of fractional bits of the grid on which stored values lie.
fixed-point.quote: Let $p$ be the number of fractional bits, so stored values lie on the grid $2^{-p}\mathbb Z[i]$.

fixed-point.name: depth
fixed-point.meaning: The number of operations in sequence since the layer began that produced a value.
fixed-point.quote: Let a value computed with $k$ operations in sequence since the layer began be said to have depth $k$.

fixed-point.name: reserved extra bits
fixed-point.meaning: The number of extra bits reserved, at least the maximal depth reached in the layer.
fixed-point.quote: Let $\Delta$ be the number of extra bits reserved, at least the maximal depth reached in the layer.

fixed-point.name: truncation
fixed-point.meaning: The truncation that drops the bits below 2^{-p} in each real and imaginary part, returning a record to the p-bit grid.
fixed-point.quote: The truncation $Q_p$ drops the bits below $2^{-p}$ in each real and imaginary part, returning the record to the $p$-bit grid, with error below $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$ per complex coefficient.

frequency-order.name: round count
frequency-order.meaning: The number of rounds of the transform, a=log_2 t.
frequency-order.quote: put $a=\log_2t$, the number of rounds (here $a$ changes meaning)

frequency-order.name: output index
frequency-order.meaning: The position of an output of the transform.
frequency-order.quote: with input positions $k$ and output index $j$ (here $j$ changes meaning: it is the position of an output of the transform)

frequency-order.name: completed rounds
frequency-order.meaning: The number of rounds completed so far.
frequency-order.quote: After $s$ rounds, $s$ being the number of completed rounds, slots $a-1,\dots,a-s$ hold frequency bits $0,\dots,s-1$ and the rest index a sequence of length $t/2^s$; the next round writes bit $s$ into slot $a-1-s$.

frequency-order.name: bit-reversal permutation
frequency-order.meaning: The permutation moving the entry at j to rev_a(j).
frequency-order.quote: Let $B_t$ be the permutation moving the entry at $j$ to $\operatorname{rev}_a(j)$

frequency-order.name: parallel butterfly
frequency-order.meaning: The parallel butterfly applying H_0 on every participating axis in one round.
frequency-order.quote: With several axes, indexed by $i$, a round applies $H_0$ on every participating axis, and $\mathcal H$ denotes this one parallel butterfly.

frequency-order.name: recordwise monomial
frequency-order.meaning: The recordwise operation multiplying each record by y^E.
frequency-order.quote: Twiddles group into one monomial $J_E$, the recordwise operation multiplying the record by $y^E$, where $E$ depends on the address, not coefficients:

gaussian-resampling.name: source length
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The length of the Fourier transform to be replaced.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Gaussian resampling expresses a Fourier transform of length $s$ through one of a nearby larger length $t$ (a power of two there), so that only power-of-two transforms need a fast algorithm.

gaussian-resampling.name: Gaussian width parameter
gaussian-resampling.meaning: An integer, with 2 <= alpha < sqrt p, that is the width parameter of the Gaussian weights.
gaussian-resampling.quote: and let $\alpha$, the width parameter of the Gaussian weights below, be an integer with $2\le\alpha<\sqrt p$.

gaussian-resampling.name: relative gap
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The relative gap t/s - 1 between the two lengths.

gaussian-resampling.name: coordinate selection
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The map from C^t to C^s that selects coordinate q_j into position j.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $C$ select coordinates from length-$t$ to length-$s$ vectors, $(Cv)_j=v_{q_j}$, and $(\mathsf Du)_j=e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}u_j$.

gaussian-resampling.name: exponent slack
gaussian-resampling.meaning: A fixed constant 0 < delta < 1/8 that is the slack in the exponents of the time bounds.

gaussian-resampling.name: output coordinate index
gaussian-resampling.meaning: A coordinate index of a vector in C^t, taken modulo t.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Define the permutations $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$ (coordinate indices $j$, $k$ taken modulo $s$, $t$), which stay in the identity, never executed as sorts.

gaussian-resampling.name: target length
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The larger length, a power of two in the application, of the transform used instead of the length-s one.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Gaussian resampling expresses a Fourier transform of length $s$ through one of a nearby larger length $t$ (a power of two there), so that only power-of-two transforms need a fast algorithm.

gaussian-resampling.name: approximate E
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The numerical approximation of E = N - I computed on D_p records.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $\widetilde E$ be the approximation of $E$ on $\mathbb D_p$ from the cited Lemma 4.11: for every $z\in\mathbb D_p^s$

hvdh-multiplier.name: factor bit length
hvdh-multiplier.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two integers given to the established multiplier.
hvdh-multiplier.quote: The established multiplier is the earlier Harvey–van der Hoeven algorithm, which multiplies two integers of $N$ bits each in $O(N\log N)$ time (this $N$ is not the bank size of the exchange network); the new algorithm calls it as an ordinary subroutine for the integer products it cannot avoid.

main-result.name: chunk-width exponent
main-result.meaning: The fixed exponent giving the chunk width K = floor(d^c); not the machine constant.
main-result.quote: The axis count is $d=\Theta(p^{\epsilon})$ and the chunk width $K=\lfloor d^{c}\rfloor$, with fixed exponents $\epsilon$ and $c$ from [Parameter and prime-length choice](parameter-choice.md); here $c$ is not the machine constant.

matrix-shear.name: fields per group
matrix-shear.meaning: The number of fields in each of the groups H and D.
matrix-shear.quote: Let $H=(H_1,\dots,H_m)$ and $D=(D_1,\dots,D_m)$ be two groups of fields, $H$ before $D$, where $m$ is the number of fields in each group.

matrix-shear.name: rank of A
matrix-shear.meaning: The rank of the rational matrix A.
matrix-shear.quote: Let $A$ be a rational $m\times m$ matrix of rank $a$ (the letter $a$ changes meaning on this page).

matrix-shear.name: shear matrix
matrix-shear.meaning: A rational m by m matrix, taken from a fixed finite set, that the shear applies.
matrix-shear.quote: Let $A$ be a rational $m\times m$ matrix of rank $a$ (the letter $a$ changes meaning on this page).

matrix-shear.name: target group
matrix-shear.meaning: The first group of m fields, which receives AD.
matrix-shear.quote: Let $H=(H_1,\dots,H_m)$ and $D=(D_1,\dots,D_m)$ be two groups of fields, $H$ before $D$, where $m$ is the number of fields in each group.

matrix-shear.name: source group
matrix-shear.meaning: The second group of m fields, which is left unchanged by the shear.
matrix-shear.quote: Let $H=(H_1,\dots,H_m)$ and $D=(D_1,\dots,D_m)$ be two groups of fields, $H$ before $D$, where $m$ is the number of fields in each group.

multidim-transform.name: axis index
multidim-transform.meaning: The index of an axis of the array, from 1 to d.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $d$ be the number of axes, $i$ an axis index with $1\le i\le d$, and $q_i$ the number of positions along axis $i$, so $\boldsymbol q=(q_1,\dots,q_d)$.

multidim-transform.name: axis position count
multidim-transform.meaning: The number of positions along axis i.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $d$ be the number of axes, $i$ an axis index with $1\le i\le d$, and $q_i$ the number of positions along axis $i$, so $\boldsymbol q=(q_1,\dots,q_d)$.

multidim-transform.name: index tuple
multidim-transform.meaning: The tuple of coordinates (j_1,...,j_d) of an entry of the array.
multidim-transform.quote: An entry of the array $u$ has an index tuple $j=(j_1,\dots,j_d)$ with $0\le j_i<q_i$.

multidim-transform.name: output index tuple
multidim-transform.meaning: An output index tuple shaped like j.
multidim-transform.quote:
With $k$ an output index tuple shaped like $j$,
$$(F_{\boldsymbol q}u)_k=\frac1{\prod_i q_i}\sum_j u_j\,e^{-2\pi i\sum_i j_ik_i/q_i}.$$

multidim-transform.name: axis operator
multidim-transform.meaning: An operator on sequences of length q_i, applied to every line along axis i.
multidim-transform.quote: For operators $G_i$ on sequences of length $q_i$, the tensor product $\bigotimes_i G_i$ applies each $G_i$ to every line along axis $i$.

multidim-transform.name: time-bound slack
multidim-transform.meaning: A fixed constant with 0<delta<1/8 that sets the slack in the exponent 3/2+delta of p in the time bound.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $p$ be the number of fractional bits of the stored values, $\alpha$ an integer resampling parameter with $2\le\alpha<\sqrt p$, and $\delta$ a fixed constant with $0<\delta<1/8$ that sets the slack in the exponent $3/2+\delta$ of $p$ in the time bound.

multidim-transform.name: resampling parameter
multidim-transform.meaning: An integer resampling parameter with 2<=alpha<sqrt p.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $p$ be the number of fractional bits of the stored values, $\alpha$ an integer resampling parameter with $2\le\alpha<\sqrt p$, and $\delta$ a fixed constant with $0<\delta<1/8$ that sets the slack in the exponent $3/2+\delta$ of $p$ in the time bound.

multidim-transform.name: source lengths
multidim-transform.meaning: The tuple of source axis lengths (s_1,...,s_d).
multidim-transform.quote: Let $\boldsymbol s=(s_1,\dots,s_d)$ and $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ be the source and padded axis lengths, $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$ the total exponent of the scalar, and, with $R$ here not the scalar ring, $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$, $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$:

multidim-transform.name: padded lengths
multidim-transform.meaning: The tuple of padded power-of-two axis lengths (t_1,...,t_d).
multidim-transform.quote: Let $\boldsymbol s=(s_1,\dots,s_d)$ and $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ be the source and padded axis lengths, $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$ the total exponent of the scalar, and, with $R$ here not the scalar ring, $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$, $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$:

multidim-transform.name: scalar exponent
multidim-transform.meaning: The total exponent 2d alpha^2 of the power of two multiplying the tensored identity.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $\boldsymbol s=(s_1,\dots,s_d)$ and $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ be the source and padded axis lengths, $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$ the total exponent of the scalar, and, with $R$ here not the scalar ring, $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$, $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$:

multidim-transform.name: source permutation
multidim-transform.meaning: The tensor product of the source index permutations P_{s_i}; here not the scalar ring.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $\boldsymbol s=(s_1,\dots,s_d)$ and $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ be the source and padded axis lengths, $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$ the total exponent of the scalar, and, with $R$ here not the scalar ring, $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$, $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$:

multidim-transform.name: padded permutation
multidim-transform.meaning: The tensor product of the index permutations P_{t_i}.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $\boldsymbol s=(s_1,\dots,s_d)$ and $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ be the source and padded axis lengths, $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$ the total exponent of the scalar, and, with $R$ here not the scalar ring, $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$, $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$:

multidim-transform.name: input map
multidim-transform.meaning: The tensor product of the one-dimensional input maps A_i.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $\boldsymbol s=(s_1,\dots,s_d)$ and $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ be the source and padded axis lengths, $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$ the total exponent of the scalar, and, with $R$ here not the scalar ring, $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$, $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$:

multidim-transform.name: output map
multidim-transform.meaning: The tensor product of the one-dimensional output maps B_{0,i}.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $\boldsymbol s=(s_1,\dots,s_d)$ and $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ be the source and padded axis lengths, $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$ the total exponent of the scalar, and, with $R$ here not the scalar ring, $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$, $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$:

multidim-transform.name: source axis permutation
multidim-transform.meaning: The index permutation of source axis i.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $P_{s_i}$ and $P_{t_i}$ be the index permutations of the source and padded axes, and $A_i$ and $B_{0,i}$ the linear input and output maps of axis $i$.

multidim-transform.name: padded axis permutation
multidim-transform.meaning: The index permutation of padded axis i.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $P_{s_i}$ and $P_{t_i}$ be the index permutations of the source and padded axes, and $A_i$ and $B_{0,i}$ the linear input and output maps of axis $i$.

multidim-transform.name: axis input map
multidim-transform.meaning: The linear input map of axis i.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $P_{s_i}$ and $P_{t_i}$ be the index permutations of the source and padded axes, and $A_i$ and $B_{0,i}$ the linear input and output maps of axis $i$.

multidim-transform.name: axis output map
multidim-transform.meaning: The linear output map of axis i.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $P_{s_i}$ and $P_{t_i}$ be the index permutations of the source and padded axes, and $A_i$ and $B_{0,i}$ the linear input and output maps of axis $i$.

multidim-transform.name: axis transform
multidim-transform.meaning: The one-dimensional normalized discrete Fourier transform of length q_i.
multidim-transform.quote: Here $F_{q_i}$ is the one-dimensional normalized [Discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) of length $q_i$, and $F_{\boldsymbol q}:=\bigotimes_iF_{q_i}$ is the tensor product of these.

multidim-transform.name: multidimensional transform
multidim-transform.meaning: The tensor product of the axis transforms F_{q_i}.
multidim-transform.quote: Here $F_{q_i}$ is the one-dimensional normalized [Discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) of length $q_i$, and $F_{\boldsymbol q}:=\bigotimes_iF_{q_i}$ is the tensor product of these.

multidim-transform.name: axis operator X
multidim-transform.meaning: An operator on axis i.
multidim-transform.quote: Operators compose axis by axis, so $(\bigotimes_i X_i)(\bigotimes_i Y_i)=\bigotimes_i X_iY_i$ for operators $X_i,Y_i$ on axis $i$, and the scalars multiply.

multidim-transform.name: axis operator Y
multidim-transform.meaning: An operator on axis i.
multidim-transform.quote: Operators compose axis by axis, so $(\bigotimes_i X_i)(\bigotimes_i Y_i)=\bigotimes_i X_iY_i$ for operators $X_i,Y_i$ on axis $i$, and the scalars multiply.

multiplication-algorithm.name: digit width
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The number of bits in one radix digit, the ceiling of log2 n.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: It takes its sizes from [Parameter and prime-length choice](parameter-choice.md): $b=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ is the digit width, $p=6b$ is the number of fractional bits, $s_i$ are distinct odd prime axis lengths with product $S$, and $t_i$ are power-of-two axis lengths with product $T$.

multiplication-algorithm.name: padded axis length
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The power-of-two length of axis i; their product is T.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: It takes its sizes from [Parameter and prime-length choice](parameter-choice.md): $b=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ is the digit width, $p=6b$ is the number of fractional bits, $s_i$ are distinct odd prime axis lengths with product $S$, and $t_i$ are power-of-two axis lengths with product $T$.

multiplication-algorithm.name: prime-axis transform
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The discrete Fourier transform on the axes s_i, normalized by 1/S.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: Let $F_{\boldsymbol s}$ be the discrete Fourier transform on the axes $s_i$, normalized by $1/S$.

multiplication-algorithm.name: padded-axis transform
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The discrete Fourier transform on the axes t_i, normalized by 1/T.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: $F_{\boldsymbol s}^+$ is the same with the opposite sign in the exponent, and $F_{\boldsymbol t}$ is the transform on the axes $t_i$, normalized by $1/T$.

multiplication-algorithm.name: normalized convolution
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The normalized cyclic convolution f*g/T.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: Let $\mathcal M_{\mathbb C}(f,g)=f*g/T$ be the normalized cyclic convolution, computed through the [Phase twist](phase-twist.md) and [Convolution from the retained transform layout](ring-convolution.md).

multiplication-algorithm.name: chirp
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The chirp array, a quadratic phase in the index.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: With the chirp array $a_{\boldsymbol j}=\exp(-\pi i\sum_i s_ij_i^2/t_i)$ and the target permutation $Q$, the [Bluestein chirp identity](chirp.md) gives $QF_{\boldsymbol t}x=\overline a\cdot\mathcal M_{\mathbb C}(a,\overline a\cdot x)$: phase, convolution with the chirp, phase.

multiplication-algorithm.name: computed chirp
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The stored approximation of the chirp a.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: The computed version uses an approximation $\widetilde a$ of $a$ and truncation $Q_p$ to $p$ fractional bits.

multiplication-algorithm.name: data operand
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The data operand after the first chirp phase.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: It forms the operand $x_0=Q_p(\overline{\widetilde a}\cdot x)$ after the first phase, then $y_0=\widetilde{\mathcal M}_{\mathbb C}(\widetilde a,x_0)$, the computed convolution, and returns $\widetilde{\mathscr C}(x)=Q_p(\overline{\widetilde a}\cdot y_0)$.

multiplication-algorithm.name: computed convolution
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The computed convolution of the chirp with the data operand.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: It forms the operand $x_0=Q_p(\overline{\widetilde a}\cdot x)$ after the first phase, then $y_0=\widetilde{\mathcal M}_{\mathbb C}(\widetilde a,x_0)$, the computed convolution, and returns $\widetilde{\mathscr C}(x)=Q_p(\overline{\widetilde a}\cdot y_0)$.

multiplication-algorithm.name: computed convolution map
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The computed approximate version of the normalized cyclic convolution.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: It forms the operand $x_0=Q_p(\overline{\widetilde a}\cdot x)$ after the first phase, then $y_0=\widetilde{\mathcal M}_{\mathbb C}(\widetilde a,x_0)$, the computed convolution, and returns $\widetilde{\mathscr C}(x)=Q_p(\overline{\widetilde a}\cdot y_0)$.

multiplication-algorithm.name: computed chirp transform
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The computed chirp transform.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: It forms the operand $x_0=Q_p(\overline{\widetilde a}\cdot x)$ after the first phase, then $y_0=\widetilde{\mathcal M}_{\mathbb C}(\widetilde a,x_0)$, the computed convolution, and returns $\widetilde{\mathscr C}(x)=Q_p(\overline{\widetilde a}\cdot y_0)$.

multiplication-algorithm.name: computed source transform
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The computed source transform: resample, chirp transform, resample, scale.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: The computed source transform $\widetilde{\mathscr F}$ applies the [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md) map $\mathcal A$, then $\widetilde{\mathscr C}$, then the map $\mathcal B_0$, then multiplies exactly by $2^\gamma$, where $\gamma$ is the resampling scale exponent; its exact counterpart $\mathscr F$ replaces each numerical routine by the exact map it approximates, giving $\mathscr F=2^\gamma\mathcal B_0QF_{\boldsymbol t}\mathcal A=RF_{\boldsymbol s}$, where $R$ is a retained permutation.

packed-bit-addition.name: source chunk
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The address chunk whose selected bits are XORed into y.
packed-bit-addition.quote: Packed selected-bit addition XORs chosen bits of a chunk $x$ into chunk $y$ (chunks here), restoring a scratch chunk $z$; the [simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-layer.md) on $d$ address chunks needs it.

packed-bit-addition.name: target chunk
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The address chunk that receives the XORs (not the ring variable).
packed-bit-addition.quote: Packed selected-bit addition XORs chosen bits of a chunk $x$ into chunk $y$ (chunks here), restoring a scratch chunk $z$; the [simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-layer.md) on $d$ address chunks needs it.

packed-bit-addition.name: scratch chunk
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The third address chunk, used as scratch and restored.
packed-bit-addition.quote: Packed selected-bit addition XORs chosen bits of a chunk $x$ into chunk $y$ (chunks here), restoring a scratch chunk $z$; the [simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-layer.md) on $d$ address chunks needs it.

packed-bit-addition.name: chunk count
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The number of address chunks the butterfly layer acts on.
packed-bit-addition.quote: Packed selected-bit addition XORs chosen bits of a chunk $x$ into chunk $y$ (chunks here), restoring a scratch chunk $z$; the [simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-layer.md) on $d$ address chunks needs it.

packed-bit-addition.name: record bits
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The number of bits in a record (not the scalar ring).
packed-bit-addition.quote: Records have $R$ bits.

packed-bit-addition.name: chunk bits
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The number of bits in an address chunk, L=fK.
packed-bit-addition.quote: A chunk has $L=fK$ bits (segment length $K\ge6$); the $f$ selected bits lie at $j_i=\rho+iK$, $0\le i<f$, with offset $\rho<K$; the goal is $y_{j_i}\leftarrow y_{j_i}\oplus x_{j_i}$.

packed-bit-addition.name: segment length
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The number of bits in a segment, and the spacing of selected positions.
packed-bit-addition.quote: A chunk has $L=fK$ bits (segment length $K\ge6$); the $f$ selected bits lie at $j_i=\rho+iK$, $0\le i<f$, with offset $\rho<K$; the goal is $y_{j_i}\leftarrow y_{j_i}\oplus x_{j_i}$.

packed-bit-addition.name: selected bits
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The number of selected bit positions in a chunk.
packed-bit-addition.quote: A chunk has $L=fK$ bits (segment length $K\ge6$); the $f$ selected bits lie at $j_i=\rho+iK$, $0\le i<f$, with offset $\rho<K$; the goal is $y_{j_i}\leftarrow y_{j_i}\oplus x_{j_i}$.

packed-bit-addition.name: offset
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The position of the lowest selected bit, 0 <= rho < K.
packed-bit-addition.quote: A chunk has $L=fK$ bits (segment length $K\ge6$); the $f$ selected bits lie at $j_i=\rho+iK$, $0\le i<f$, with offset $\rho<K$; the goal is $y_{j_i}\leftarrow y_{j_i}\oplus x_{j_i}$.

packed-bit-addition.name: selected position
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The position j_i = rho + iK of the i-th selected bit.
packed-bit-addition.quote: A chunk has $L=fK$ bits (segment length $K\ge6$); the $f$ selected bits lie at $j_i=\rho+iK$, $0\le i<f$, with offset $\rho<K$; the goal is $y_{j_i}\leftarrow y_{j_i}\oplus x_{j_i}$.

packed-bit-addition.name: address count
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The number of addresses.
packed-bit-addition.quote: Let $M$ count addresses, $V=MR$, and $A_{\rm rect}=\lceil\log_2(2V)\rceil$ bound counter lengths.

packed-bit-addition.name: volume
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The number of bits stored, MR.
packed-bit-addition.quote: Let $M$ count addresses, $V=MR$, and $A_{\rm rect}=\lceil\log_2(2V)\rceil$ bound counter lengths.

packed-bit-addition.name: counter length
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The bit length of counters, ceil(log2(2V)).
packed-bit-addition.quote: Let $M$ count addresses, $V=MR$, and $A_{\rm rect}=\lceil\log_2(2V)\rceil$ bound counter lengths.

packed-bit-addition.name: control
packed-bit-addition.meaning: A Boolean control.
packed-bit-addition.quote: For a Boolean control $c$ and integers $u,w$, $c[P]$ is $c$ if $P$ holds, else $0$.

packed-bit-addition.name: first integer
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The integer on which the parity-conditioned additions act first (a segment of y).
packed-bit-addition.quote: For a Boolean control $c$ and integers $u,w$, $c[P]$ is $c$ if $P$ holds, else $0$.

packed-bit-addition.name: second integer
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The auxiliary integer to be restored (a segment of z).
packed-bit-addition.quote: For a Boolean control $c$ and integers $u,w$, $c[P]$ is $c$ if $P$ holds, else $0$.

packed-bit-addition.name: guard of y
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The segment value of y divided by two, rounded down.
packed-bit-addition.quote: For $0\le i<f-1$, the $K$ bits of $y$ from $j_i$ give a segment $u_i=2g_i+a_i$ and those of $z$ give $w_i=2h_i+b_i$, with bits $a_i,b_i$, guard values $g_i,h_i\in\{0,\dots,2^{K-1}-1\}$, and control $c_i=x_{j_i}$.

packed-bit-addition.name: guard of z
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The segment value of z divided by two, rounded down.
packed-bit-addition.quote: For $0\le i<f-1$, the $K$ bits of $y$ from $j_i$ give a segment $u_i=2g_i+a_i$ and those of $z$ give $w_i=2h_i+b_i$, with bits $a_i,b_i$, guard values $g_i,h_i\in\{0,\dots,2^{K-1}-1\}$, and control $c_i=x_{j_i}$.

packed-bit-addition.name: low bit of y
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The lowest bit of the i-th segment of y.
packed-bit-addition.quote: For $0\le i<f-1$, the $K$ bits of $y$ from $j_i$ give a segment $u_i=2g_i+a_i$ and those of $z$ give $w_i=2h_i+b_i$, with bits $a_i,b_i$, guard values $g_i,h_i\in\{0,\dots,2^{K-1}-1\}$, and control $c_i=x_{j_i}$.

packed-bit-addition.quote: For $0\le i<f-1$, the $K$ bits of $y$ from $j_i$ give a segment $u_i=2g_i+a_i$ and those of $z$ give $w_i=2h_i+b_i$, with bits $a_i,b_i$, guard values $g_i,h_i\in\{0,\dots,2^{K-1}-1\}$, and control $c_i=x_{j_i}$.

packed-bit-addition.name: packed map
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The composition of the eight packed cyclic shifts.
packed-bit-addition.quote: Each is a cyclic shift of a whole chunk by an offset independent of the target chunk, hence a bijection of the addresses; $S_0$ composes the eight.

packed-bit-addition.name: exceptional set
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The addresses where some guard of y or z lies outside [10, 2^{K-1}-11].
packed-bit-addition.quote: Let $\mathcal B$ (exceptional addresses) be those where a guard of $y$ or $z$ fails $10\le g\le2^{K-1}-11$.

packed-bit-addition.name: ideal map
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The permutation that performs the required XORs at j_0..j_{f-2}.
packed-bit-addition.quote: Off $\mathcal B$ each segment lies in $[20,2^K-21]$, so displacement eight stays in $[0,2^K-1]$: no segment carries into or borrows from a neighbour, and $S_0$ equals the ideal map $T_0$ XORing at $j_0,\dots,j_{f-2}$.

packed-bit-addition.name: bad fraction
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The bound min{1, 80(f-1)2^{-K}} on the fraction of exceptional addresses.
packed-bit-addition.quote: Guards are equidistributed at every spectator choice, so a union bound over $2(f-1)$ guards gives $|\mathcal B|\le\delta_{\rm bad}M$ with $\delta_{\rm bad}=\min\{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}\}$.

packed-bit-addition.name: swap exponent

packed-bit-addition.quote: It performs rotations as [controlled shifts](controlled-shifts.md) costing $O(V)$ and swaps as [chunk interchanges](address-interchange.md) costing $O(VL^\tau)$ for fixed exponent $\tau<1$.

packed-bit-addition.name: precision
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The number of precision bits of the records.
packed-bit-addition.quote: With $p$ the precision bits, both vanish when $A_{\rm rect}=O(p)$, $R$ exceeds every polynomial in $p$, $f\le d\le p$ and $K/\log p\to\infty$, so the cost is $O(V(L^\tau+1))$.

parameter-choice.name: relative distance
parameter-choice.meaning: The relative distance 1/(4d) of each prime s_i below t_i.
parameter-choice.quote: Put $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$ and $\eta=1/(4d)$, the relative distance of each prime $s_i$ below $t_i$.

parameter-choice.name: axis relative gap
parameter-choice.meaning: The relative gap t_i/s_i - 1 of axis i.
parameter-choice.quote: With the relative gap $\theta_i=t_i/s_i-1\ge\eta/(1-\eta)>\eta$ we get $\alpha^4\theta_i>12d^2b/(4d)=3db\ge6b=p$, the separation hypothesis of the resampling lemma; also $t_i\le r\le T<2^p$.

parameter-choice.name: real argument
parameter-choice.meaning: A real number, the length at which the prime interval is taken.
parameter-choice.quote: As $\lceil x\rceil\le2x$ for real $x\ge1$ and $8\sqrt{12}<28$, then $\gamma<28d^2\sqrt b\le28b^{1/2+2\epsilon}\le28b^{2/3}$, so $2\le\alpha<\sqrt p$ eventually and $\gamma=o(b)$.

parameter-choice.name: integer in interval
parameter-choice.meaning: An integer, in the prime interval.
parameter-choice.quote: By the prime-interval lemma, for $0<\eta<1/4$ and real $x>e^{2/\eta}$ the interval of integers $q$ with $(1-2\eta)x<q\le(1-\eta)x$ contains at least $\eta x/(2\log x)$ primes

phase-frames.name: binary vector
phase-frames.meaning: A vector of F_2^m; in the main argument a basis vector of an edge residual. Here v does not mean the triple count.
phase-frames.quote: Labels are subspaces of $\mathbb F_2^m$ ($m$ the label dimension), and $u,v,w,z$ are vectors of $\mathbb F_2^m$ here.

phase-frames.name: phase exponent
phase-frames.meaning: The weight modulo four of the projection of an address x onto the label U.
phase-frames.quote: For a label $U$ put $q_U(x)=\operatorname{wt}(P_Ux)\bmod 4$, with the projection taken over $\mathbb F_2$.

phase-frames.name: phase frame
phase-frames.meaning: The operator on arrays attached to the label U.
phase-frames.quote: The phase frame is $\mathcal C_U=H^{\otimes m}\operatorname{diag}_x(i^{q_U(x)})H^{\otimes m}$, with Gaussian-dyadic entries.

phase-frames.name: translation
phase-frames.meaning: The operator shifting an array by the vector v: (X_v f)(x)=f(x+v).
phase-frames.quote: Let $X_v$ be the translation $(X_vf)(x)=f(x+v)$, and $C=H\operatorname{diag}(1,i)H=aI+bX$ with $a=\frac{1+i}{2}$, $b=\frac{1-i}{2}$, where $H=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$.

phase-frames.name: residual basis
phase-frames.meaning: An orthonormal basis of the edge residual E.
phase-frames.quote: Take an edge from $U$ to $V=U\perp E$, where $E$, the edge residual, has orthonormal basis $\mathcal B$.

phase-frames.name: edge residual
phase-frames.meaning: The subspace added to U to reach V, orthogonal to U; here E is not the first space of a tensor product.
phase-frames.quote: Take an edge from $U$ to $V=U\perp E$, where $E$, the edge residual, has orthonormal basis $\mathcal B$.

phase-frames.name: phase sign
phase-frames.meaning: The coefficient +1 or -1 modulo four of a basis vector's phase, including the edge direction.
phase-frames.quote: Each term is therefore $\varepsilon[v\cdot x]$ with $\varepsilon=\pm1$ modulo four, the sign including the edge direction.

phase-frames.name: sign matrix
phase-frames.quote: With $Z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$ we have $ZXZ=-X$ and $C^{-1}=bI+aX$; since $ib=a$ and $ia=-b$, $C=iZC^{-1}Z$.

phase-frames.name: sign correction
phase-frames.meaning: The tensor product of Z on the 27 coordinates of supp(u) in every column and the identity elsewhere.
phase-frames.quote: Let $Z_{a,k}$ be $Z$ on those 27 coordinates in every column.

phase-frames.name: column count
phase-frames.meaning: The number of columns of an address; here k changes meaning from the fixed-point page.
phase-frames.quote: For $k$ columns (an address is a $k$-tuple; $k$ changes meaning from the fixed-point page), [Frames on wire arrays](array-frames.md) gives each role the $k$th tensor power of the sink frame times the inverse source frame, with $X_a,Y_a$ exchanged.

phase-kernel.name: kernel coefficient a
phase-kernel.meaning: The complex constant (1+i)/2, the coefficient of the identity in C.
phase-kernel.quote: Let $a=\frac{1+i}{2}$ and $b=\frac{1-i}{2}$ be two complex constants (these letters have other meanings on other pages).

phase-kernel.name: kernel coefficient b
phase-kernel.meaning: The complex constant (1-i)/2, the coefficient of the bit flip in C.
phase-kernel.quote: Let $a=\frac{1+i}{2}$ and $b=\frac{1-i}{2}$ be two complex constants (these letters have other meanings on other pages).

phase-kernel.name: identity matrix

phase-kernel.name: bit flip
phase-kernel.meaning: The 2 by 2 matrix swapping the two entries of a pair.
phase-kernel.quote: Let $I$ be the $2\times 2$ identity matrix, and let $X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ be the bit flip, which swaps the two entries of a pair $(u,v)$.

phase-kernel.name: phase matrix

phase-kernel.quote: Let $\mathsf S=\operatorname{diag}(1,i)$ be the phase matrix that multiplies the second entry of a pair by $i$.

phase-kernel.name: normalized Hadamard matrix
phase-kernel.meaning: The matrix sqrt(2) H_0, symmetric with H squared equal to the identity.
phase-kernel.quote: Let $H_0=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$ be the matrix of the averaging and differencing step $(u,v)\mapsto\bigl(\tfrac{u+v}{2},\tfrac{u-v}{2}\bigr)$, and let $H=\sqrt2\,H_0$ be the normalized Hadamard matrix, which is symmetric and satisfies $H^2=I$.

phase-kernel.name: two-point butterfly

phase-twist.name: twist root

phase-twist.name: twist map
phase-twist.meaning: The ring isomorphism from the cyclic ring to the negacyclic ring sending x_d to zeta y.

phase-twist.name: coefficient index

phase-twist.name: second coefficient index

phase-twist.quote: Here $k$ and $l$ index coefficients, not operations.

phase-twist.name: wrapped position

phase-twist.name: wrap indicator
phase-twist.meaning: Zero or one according to whether k+l wrapped past r.
phase-twist.quote: Take $k,l<r$ and write $k+l=j+hr$, with $j<r$ the resulting position and $h\in\{0,1\}$ the wrap indicator.

phase-twist.name: record reading
phase-twist.meaning: The map reading each line along the last axis as a polynomial in R_r.
phase-twist.quote: $\iota$ reads each line $(f_{\boldsymbol j,k})_k$ as the polynomial $\sum_k f_{\boldsymbol j,k}y^k$, giving an array of $M$ records in $\mathcal R_r$.

phase-twist.name: diagonal twist
phase-twist.meaning: The maps multiplying entry k of each line by zeta^{+-k}.
phase-twist.quote: Let $(D_\pm f)_{\boldsymbol j,k}=\zeta^{\pm k}f_{\boldsymbol j,k}$ multiply entry $k$ of each line by $\zeta^{\pm k}$.

phase-twist.name: ring convolution
phase-twist.meaning: Normalized convolution of the first d-1 axes over R_r, including division by T.
phase-twist.quote: Let $\mathcal M_r$ be the ring convolution of [Convolution from the retained transform layout](ring-convolution.md): it convolves the first $d-1$ axes over $\mathcal R_r$, dividing by $T$.

phase-twist.name: sup norm

phase-twist.quote: Write $\|f\|$ for the sup norm of an array $f$: the largest modulus of a scalar coefficient.

precision-recovery.meaning: The error bound, in units of h_p, of a source transform.
precision-recovery.quote: As $2dp^2<TL$ eventually, error is under $E_sh_p$, $E_s=9\cdot2^\gamma TL$.

precision-recovery.name: scaled digit array

precision-recovery.quote: Here $u,v$ denote the scaled digit arrays (letters redefined): a digit $a$ is stored as $a2^{-b-2}$, norm under $1/4$.

precision-recovery.quote: Let $U,V_1$ be their exact source transforms and $\widetilde U,\widetilde V_1$ the computed ones, of norm under $.26$.

precision-recovery.quote: Let $U,V_1$ be their exact source transforms and $\widetilde U,\widetilde V_1$ the computed ones, of norm under $.26$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: first input
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The first of the two integers being multiplied.

radix-digit-reduction.name: second input
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The second of the two integers being multiplied.

radix-digit-reduction.name: input bit length
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The number of bits in each input.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $n$ be the number of bits in each input, and let $b=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ be the number of bits in one digit, so $n\le 2^b$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: digit width
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The number of bits in one radix digit.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $n$ be the number of bits in each input, and let $b=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ be the number of bits in one digit, so $n\le 2^b$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: padded length
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: A power of two with 4n/b <= T < 8n/b.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: $T$ is the padded length, a power of two with $4n/b\le T<8n/b$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: convolution length
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The length of the cyclic convolution, a product of distinct odd primes with T/2 < S < T.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: $S$ is the length of the cyclic convolution, a product of distinct odd primes with $T/2<S<T$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: digit count
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The number of radix-2^b digits in each input.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $q=\lceil n/b\rceil$ be the number of digits in each input, padding with leading zeros.

radix-digit-reduction.name: digit of u
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The i-th radix-2^b digit of u, an integer below 2^b.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Write $u=\sum_{i=0}^{q-1}u_i2^{bi}$ and $v=\sum_{k=0}^{q-1}v_k2^{bk}$, where the digits $u_i$ and $v_k$ are integers with $0\le u_i,v_k<2^b$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: digit of v
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The k-th radix-2^b digit of v, an integer below 2^b.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Write $u=\sum_{i=0}^{q-1}u_i2^{bi}$ and $v=\sum_{k=0}^{q-1}v_k2^{bk}$, where the digits $u_i$ and $v_k$ are integers with $0\le u_i,v_k<2^b$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: polynomial variable
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The variable of the digit polynomials, evaluated at 2^b to recover the integers.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $x$ be a polynomial variable, and form the polynomials in $x$ with the $u_i$ and with the $v_k$ as coefficients.

radix-digit-reduction.name: product coefficient
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The coefficient of x^j in the product of the digit polynomials.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $c_j=\sum_{i+k=j}u_iv_k$ be the coefficient of $x^j$ in that product.

rank-recurrence.name: call parameter
rank-recurrence.meaning: The parameter of a recursive call: the number of digits per interchanged chunk, or the number of selected axes in a butterfly layer.
rank-recurrence.quote: A call has a parameter $f$, the number of digits per interchanged chunk or of selected axes, and a volume $V$.

rank-recurrence.name: slot count
rank-recurrence.meaning: The number of size-f slots into which a call at parameter mf cuts its parameter, equal to 10^6, the label-space dimension.
rank-recurrence.quote: A call at parameter $mf$, with $m=10^6$ (the label-space dimension) slots of size $f$, deals its rows into $W$ streams of volume $V/W$, one per wire of a fixed bit or complex [exchange network](exchange-network.md).

rank-recurrence.name: number of smaller calls
rank-recurrence.meaning: The number of calls at parameter f made by a call at parameter mf: the total rank of the frame changes over all edges of the network.
rank-recurrence.quote: So the call makes $s$ calls at parameter $f$, each on volume $V/W$, where $s$ is the total edge rank.

rank-recurrence.name: cost per unit volume
rank-recurrence.meaning: F(f) is the running time of a call at parameter f divided by the volume of its data.
rank-recurrence.quote: With $F(f)$ the time per unit volume at parameter $f$, these cost $s(V/W)F(f)$.

rank-recurrence.name: recursion depth
rank-recurrence.meaning: The number of recursion levels between the top call and the nodes considered.
rank-recurrence.quote: Unrolling through $\log_m f$ levels ($f$ a power of $m$), with depth $j$ (here counting levels) contributing $(s/W)^j$, gives $F(f)=O\big(\sum_{j=0}^{\log_m f}(s/W)^j\big)$.

rank-recurrence.name: saving exponent
rank-recurrence.meaning: A fixed exponent below 1 with s/W < m^tau, which makes an interchange cost O(V f^tau); here tau = 1 - 2^{-50}.
rank-recurrence.quote: If $s/W<m^\tau$ with fixed $\tau<1$, this is $O(f^\tau)$: if $s/W\le1$ there are $1+\log_m f$ terms of at most $1$; otherwise the last term, below $m^{\tau\log_m f}=f^\tau$, dominates the geometric sum.

rank-recurrence.name: relative rank deficit
rank-recurrence.meaning: The fraction (Wm - s)/(Wm) by which the number of smaller calls s falls short of Wm.
rank-recurrence.quote: Write $s/W=m(1-\eta)$, with $\eta$ now the relative deficit $(Wm-s)/(Wm)$.

retained-permutations.meaning: The tuple of the prime axis lengths $s_i$.

retained-permutations.name: padded length tuple
retained-permutations.meaning: The tuple of the power-of-two axis lengths $t_i$.

retained-permutations.meaning: The transform of a vector of q entries with the exponent's sign reversed and the same factor 1/q as F_q, so that F_q^+F_q=I/q.

retained-permutations.name: unit

retained-permutations.name: summation index

retained-permutations.name: setup degree

retained-permutations.name: largest padded length
retained-permutations.meaning: The largest axis length, $2^\ell$, each $t_i$ being $t_{\max}/2$ or $t_{\max}$.

retained-permutations.name: first array
retained-permutations.meaning: A complex array (not an integer) in the resampling and convolution identities of this page.
retained-permutations.quote: ($u,v$ are complex arrays here, not integers)

retained-permutations.name: second array
retained-permutations.meaning: A complex array (not an integer) in the resampling and convolution identities of this page.
retained-permutations.quote: ($u,v$ are complex arrays here, not integers)

ring-convolution.name: number of records
ring-convolution.meaning: The number of polynomial records, one per cyclic address of the remaining axes.
ring-convolution.quote: Let $M=\prod_i t_i$ be the number of records, $T=rM$ the number of complex coefficients, and $*$ cyclic convolution.

ring-convolution.name: number of coefficients
ring-convolution.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in an array, T = rM.
ring-convolution.quote: Let $M=\prod_i t_i$ be the number of records, $T=rM$ the number of complex coefficients, and $*$ cyclic convolution.

ring-convolution.name: forward transform
ring-convolution.quote: Let $F^-$, $F^+$ be the forward and opposite synthetic transforms.

ring-convolution.name: opposite transform
ring-convolution.quote: Let $F^-$, $F^+$ be the forward and opposite synthetic transforms.

ring-convolution.name: pointwise product
ring-convolution.meaning: The pointwise product of records, P(u,v) = uv/r.

ring-convolution.name: layout permutation
ring-convolution.meaning: The permutation of records produced by the tape layout.
ring-convolution.quote: Perform both forward transforms and retain their common $LB$ order, with $L$ the layout permutation of records and $B$ the bit-reversal order.

ring-convolution.name: bit-reversal order
ring-convolution.meaning: The bit-reversal order in which forward outputs are written.
ring-convolution.quote: Perform both forward transforms and retain their common $LB$ order, with $L$ the layout permutation of records and $B$ the bit-reversal order.

ring-convolution.name: opposite map
ring-convolution.meaning: The exact counterpart F^+ B^{-1} L^{-1} of the opposite procedure.
ring-convolution.quote: Their exact counterparts are $LBF^-$ and the opposite map $\mathcal T_+=F^+B^{-1}L^{-1}$; permuting records preserves the norm, so $\mathcal T_+$ is a contraction.

ring-convolution.name: log of record length
ring-convolution.meaning: The base-2 logarithm of the record length r.
ring-convolution.quote: With $\ell=\log_2r$, each procedure maps disk grid arrays to disk grid arrays with error less than $\delta=\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}$

ring-convolution.name: transform error
ring-convolution.meaning: The error bound sqrt2 * l * 2^{-p} of each forward or opposite procedure.
ring-convolution.quote: With $\ell=\log_2r$, each procedure maps disk grid arrays to disk grid arrays with error less than $\delta=\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}$

ring-convolution.name: truncation error
ring-convolution.meaning: The error bound sqrt2 * 2^{-p} for one truncation.
ring-convolution.quote: truncated by $Q_p$ to $p$ bits of precision, which changes it by less than $\eta=\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$ without raising the norm

ring-convolution.name: layout chunk width
ring-convolution.meaning: The width of the address chunks used by the tape layout.
ring-convolution.quote: Each transform, and the final linear scaling, costs $O(Tp[dK+pK^{\tau-1}+\ell d^{\lambda'}])$, with $K$ the layout chunk width and $\tau,\lambda'$ exponents from the cost lemma.

ring-y.name: ring variable
ring-y.meaning: The indeterminate of the polynomials; it satisfies y^r = -1 in the ring.
ring-y.quote: Write $\mathcal R_r=\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ for it, where $y$ is the ring variable, the indeterminate of the polynomials, and $r$ is the record length, the number of complex coefficients in a polynomial of the ring, always a power of two with $r\geq 2$.

ring-y.name: record length
ring-y.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in a polynomial of the ring, always a power of two.
ring-y.quote: Write $\mathcal R_r=\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ for it, where $y$ is the ring variable, the indeterminate of the polynomials, and $r$ is the record length, the number of complex coefficients in a polynomial of the ring, always a power of two with $r\geq 2$.

signed-packing.name: packing base
signed-packing.meaning: The base 2^{4p} at which the polynomials are evaluated.

signed-packing.name: signed evaluation integer
signed-packing.meaning: The integer obtained by evaluating the integer-coefficient polynomial u at B_0.
signed-packing.quote: let $A_u=u(B_0)=\sum_{j<r}u_jB_0^j$ be the signed evaluation integer

signed-packing.name: carry
signed-packing.meaning: The carry, in {-1,0}, into block j when forming A_u.
signed-packing.quote: scan the coefficients with a carry $\gamma_j$

signed-packing.name: block
signed-packing.meaning: The residue of u_j plus the carry modulo B_0, the j-th block of 4p bits of A_u.
signed-packing.quote: Let $d_j\in[0,B_0)$ be the residue of $u_j+\gamma_j$ modulo $B_0$

signed-packing.name: product coefficient
signed-packing.meaning: The coefficient of y^j in the ordinary product h=ac of integer polynomials.

signed-packing.name: extraction carry
signed-packing.meaning: The carry into block j during extraction, in {0,1}.
signed-packing.quote: let $\rho_j$ be the carry into block $j$

signed-packing.name: reduced coefficient
signed-packing.meaning: The Gaussian integer coefficient of y^j after reduction modulo y^r+1.
signed-packing.quote: Let $H_j$ be the resulting Gaussian integer coefficient.

simultaneous-layer.name: selected chunk count
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The number of address chunks carrying a selected bit.
simultaneous-layer.quote: The simultaneous butterfly layer applies $H_0$ coefficientwise to one bit of each of $D\le d$ address chunks of $K$ bits $(d$ bounds their number) in time $O(Vd^{\lambda'}),$ $\lambda'<1,$ instead of $D$ passes.

simultaneous-layer.name: chunk bound
simultaneous-layer.meaning: An upper bound on the number of chunks a layer acts on.
simultaneous-layer.quote: The simultaneous butterfly layer applies $H_0$ coefficientwise to one bit of each of $D\le d$ address chunks of $K$ bits $(d$ bounds their number) in time $O(Vd^{\lambda'}),$ $\lambda'<1,$ instead of $D$ passes.

simultaneous-layer.name: record array
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The array of records, a function of the address x.
simultaneous-layer.quote: For records $z$ at addresses $x$ with selected bits $x_1,\dots,x_D,$ $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$ with $(\mathcal S_Dz)(x)=i^{x_1+\dots+x_D}z(x),$ all exact Gaussian dyadic: $b^D=(-i/2)^{\lfloor D/2\rfloor}b^{D\bmod2}$ is a shift, a phase and at most one factor $b.$

simultaneous-layer.name: address
simultaneous-layer.meaning: An address of the array, with selected bits x_1,...,x_D.
simultaneous-layer.quote: For records $z$ at addresses $x$ with selected bits $x_1,\dots,x_D,$ $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$ with $(\mathcal S_Dz)(x)=i^{x_1+\dots+x_D}z(x),$ all exact Gaussian dyadic: $b^D=(-i/2)^{\lfloor D/2\rfloor}b^{D\bmod2}$ is a shift, a phase and at most one factor $b.$

simultaneous-layer.name: phase diagonal
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The diagonal operator multiplying the record at address x by i^{x_1+...+x_D}.
simultaneous-layer.quote: For records $z$ at addresses $x$ with selected bits $x_1,\dots,x_D,$ $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$ with $(\mathcal S_Dz)(x)=i^{x_1+\dots+x_D}z(x),$ all exact Gaussian dyadic: $b^D=(-i/2)^{\lfloor D/2\rfloor}b^{D\bmod2}$ is a shift, a phase and at most one factor $b.$

simultaneous-layer.name: group axis count
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The number of axes in a group, e = mf.
simultaneous-layer.quote: A group of $e=mf$ axes has $m$ slots of $f$ axes; a column holds one bit per slot, in $\mathbb F_2^m.$

simultaneous-layer.name: slot index
simultaneous-layer.meaning: Index of a slot, and of the residual basis vector placed on it.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Each edge changes frame by $\prod_hC_{v_h}^{\eta_h}$ per column (residual basis $v_h,$ $\eta_h=\pm1,$ $C_v=aI+bX_v,$ $X_v$ shifting a column by $v).$

simultaneous-layer.name: residual vector
simultaneous-layer.meaning: A vector of a basis of the edge's residual space, in F_2^m.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Each edge changes frame by $\prod_hC_{v_h}^{\eta_h}$ per column (residual basis $v_h,$ $\eta_h=\pm1,$ $C_v=aI+bX_v,$ $X_v$ shifting a column by $v).$

simultaneous-layer.name: edge sign
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The sign +1 or -1 of the kernel exponent attached to residual vector v_h.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Each edge changes frame by $\prod_hC_{v_h}^{\eta_h}$ per column (residual basis $v_h,$ $\eta_h=\pm1,$ $C_v=aI+bX_v,$ $X_v$ shifting a column by $v).$

simultaneous-layer.name: shifted kernel
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The matrix aI+bX_v, the kernel C applied along the column direction v.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Each edge changes frame by $\prod_hC_{v_h}^{\eta_h}$ per column (residual basis $v_h,$ $\eta_h=\pm1,$ $C_v=aI+bX_v,$ $X_v$ shifting a column by $v).$

simultaneous-layer.name: column shift
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The operator shifting the address of a column by v.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Each edge changes frame by $\prod_hC_{v_h}^{\eta_h}$ per column (residual basis $v_h,$ $\eta_h=\pm1,$ $C_v=aI+bX_v,$ $X_v$ shifting a column by $v).$

simultaneous-layer.name: basis matrix
simultaneous-layer.meaning: An invertible binary m by m matrix whose first columns are the residual vectors v_h.
simultaneous-layer.quote: For invertible $G$ with first columns $v_h$ and $\mathcal P_G:x\mapsto Gx,$ $\mathcal P_GX_v\mathcal P_G^{-1}=X_{Gv}$

simultaneous-layer.name: basis permutation
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The address permutation moving a column value x to Gx.
simultaneous-layer.quote: For invertible $G$ with first columns $v_h$ and $\mathcal P_G:x\mapsto Gx,$ $\mathcal P_GX_v\mathcal P_G^{-1}=X_{Gv}$

simultaneous-layer.name: standard basis vector
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The h-th standard basis vector of F_2^m.
simultaneous-layer.quote: , so the edge change is $\mathcal P_G(\prod_hC_{e_h}^{\eta_h})\mathcal P_G^{-1}$ $(e_h$ standard basis).

simultaneous-layer.name: sign matrix
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The diagonal matrix diag(1,-1).
simultaneous-layer.quote: As $(C^{-1})^{\otimes f}=(-i)^fZ^{\otimes f}C^{\otimes f}Z^{\otimes f},$ $Z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1),$ inverse children need only signs and phases.

simultaneous-layer.name: row quotient
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The quotient of a row index on division by W.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Row $Wq+w$ (quotient $q,$ remainder $w<W)$ goes to wire role $w,$ so children have volume $V/W.$

simultaneous-layer.name: row remainder
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The remainder of a row index modulo W, which is the wire role.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Row $Wq+w$ (quotient $q,$ remainder $w<W)$ goes to wire role $w,$ so children have volume $V/W.$

simultaneous-layer.name: row chunk count
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The number of leading chunks whose bits form the row index.
simultaneous-layer.quote: The first $q_0=\lceil\log_2W\rceil\lceil\log_m(2d)\rceil$ chunks, $q_0$ counting chunks, are done individually in $O(V\log d)$ (all chunks if $D\le q_0);$ their bits form a row index of range $2^{q_0K}\ge W^{\lceil\log_md\rceil},$ zero-padded at most doubling volume.

simultaneous-layer.name: step ratio
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The ratio s/W, at most m^sigma.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Take $\sigma<1$ with $\gamma=s/W\le m^\sigma,$ $K\le d^c$ $(c>0$ fixed), and $\lambda$ with $\max\{\tau,\sigma\}<\lambda<1,$ $\tau(1+c/\beta)<\lambda.$

simultaneous-layer.name: level index
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The index of a recursion level, counted from 0.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Levels indexed by $j\ge0$ sum to $O(e^\lambda)\sum_{j\ge0}(\gamma/m^\lambda)^j=O(e^\lambda).$

simultaneous-layer.name: leaf chunks
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The number of active chunks in a leaf at level j, e/m^j.
simultaneous-layer.quote: A leaf at level $j$ has $u=e/m^j<d^\beta$ chunks and $\gamma^j\le(e/u)^\sigma,$ so leaves add $O(\gamma^ju)\le O(e^\sigma d^{\beta(1-\sigma)}).$

simultaneous-layer.quote: Let $A(e)$ bound operations along a chain from an input to an intermediate coefficient.

simultaneous-layer.name: invocation bound

simultaneous-layer.quote: One invocation adds fewer than $E=64(W+m+1)^3$ (gates, corrections, $s<Wm),$ and chains concatenate the $s$ children:

simultaneous-layer.name: bound

simultaneous-layer.quote: Since $s\xi+E\le B\xi$ for $\xi\ge1,$ $B=s+E,$ over at most $\lceil\log_md\rceil$ levels, with $\nu=\min\{j\ge1:m^j\ge B\},$ $A(e)\le8B^2d^{\nu+1}.$

simultaneous-layer.name: recurrence base
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The sum s+E.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Since $s\xi+E\le B\xi$ for $\xi\ge1,$ $B=s+E,$ over at most $\lceil\log_md\rceil$ levels, with $\nu=\min\{j\ge1:m^j\ge B\},$ $A(e)\le8B^2d^{\nu+1}.$

simultaneous-layer.name: depth exponent

simultaneous-layer.quote: Since $s\xi+E\le B\xi$ for $\xi\ge1,$ $B=s+E,$ over at most $\lceil\log_md\rceil$ levels, with $\nu=\min\{j\ge1:m^j\ge B\},$ $A(e)\le8B^2d^{\nu+1}.$

simultaneous-layer.name: guard constant

simultaneous-layer.quote: Adding pieces, diagonals and $b^D$ stays below $\Delta=\lceil C_0d^{C_1}\rceil,$ $C_0=128mB^2,$ $C_1=\max\{20,\nu+3\}=20$ here.

simultaneous-layer.name: chain depth
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The number of operations along a chain, the depth of a value.
simultaneous-layer.quote: For disk inputs on $2^{-p}\mathbb Z[i]$ and chain depth $\ell,$ values lie in $2^{-(p+\ell)}\mathbb Z[i]$ with modulus at most $2^\ell,$ by induction: addition doubles modulus, halving adds a denominator bit.

simultaneous-layer.name: axis exponent

simultaneous-layer.quote: For $d=\Theta(p^\epsilon),$ fixed $\epsilon$ with $\epsilon C_1<1,$ $\Delta=o(p):$ width $O(p).$

subspace-labels.name: a triple

address-interchange.quote: Within each prefix, rows are split into role streams by [stream scans](stream-ops.md): row $Wx+w-1$ goes to stream $w$ as row $x$.

array-frames.quote: They extend the [linear exchange network with restored scratch wires](exchange-network.md) from scalars to arrays while keeping each edge cheap.

butterfly.quote: Repeated over the address bits of an array, with twiddle multiplications between layers, it computes the [Discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) of an array in $\log_2 t$ layers instead of $t^2$ operations.

chirp.quote: The Bluestein chirp identity rewrites a permuted [Discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) as a pointwise chirp phase, a cyclic convolution, and another chirp phase, so the target permutation of resampling is absorbed into the convolution and never executed as a sort.
The permuted transform is thus reduced to one [Cyclic convolution](convolution.md) of length $T$ between two pointwise phase multiplications.

conjecture.quote: The conjecture is stated for the [Fixed finite-tape machine model](machine-model.md): a multitape Turing machine with a fixed alphabet and a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes.
